clue.text: Battle later developed into chase

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go into the middle of the other word, which wraps round them

parts.note: to chase a lover is to woo them

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A military history note: a skirmish that later grew into a full pursuit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chase' looks like pursuit to go with the battle, but here it means courting a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: Waterloo is the 1815 clash where Wellington and Blucher defeated Napoleon, a famous military engagement.

clue.text: One would have the Sun going round the Earth

indicators.note: one word circling another means it wraps around it on both sides

parts.note: Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of the old geocentric model, with the sun orbiting our planet.
explanation.walkthrough: SOL wraps round I to make SOIL. The astronomy surface hides that 'the Earth' here means ground, not the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil is the earth in the sense of the ground or dirt in which plants grow.

clue.text: Twelve did wrong in a month

indicators.note: the muddled letters are placed inside the month's name

parts.note: May is a month of the year

indicators.note: done wrong, the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Twelve people, perhaps a jury, behaved badly during one month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twelve' reads like a group of people, but it is the time of day.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday is twelve o'clock noon, the hour when the clock shows twelve in daytime.

clue.text: This beast can jump barrier by a ruin

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: ruin the short words and their letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A beast able to leap a fence and leave it in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jump barrier' reads as one phrase, but the definition ends at 'jump' and 'barrier' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaby is a small kangaroo-like marsupial that moves by hopping, so it can certainly jump.

clue.text: Draw diffused ray, perhaps a bit on the short side

definitions.text: a bit on the short side

indicators.note: something diffused is spread about, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a ray is one example of a fish

explanation.surface: An instruction to sketch a scattered beam of light, which comes out rather stubby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' sounds like light beside 'diffused', but it is the flat sea creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwarfish describes something small or stunted, so a little below normal height.

clue.text: Lots of rain could start to bring rust somehow

indicators.note: arranged somehow means in some unstated new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of bring
taken as written

explanation.surface: Heavy rain might somehow cause metal to corrode.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloudburst is a sudden, very heavy downpour, a great deal of water falling at once.

clue.text: Fish in sea round both sides

indicators.note: one word going round the other wraps it on both sides

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
right and left, abbreviated R and L

explanation.surface: A fish swimming in the sea, circling from side to side.
explanation.walkthrough: The main is an old poetic word for the open ocean, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The marlin is a large ocean game fish with a long spear-like bill.

clue.text: City Hall — first class, about to receive a king

parts.note: a salon is a reception hall

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
receiving something means taking it inside

parts.note: A1 means first class, with the 1 read as I
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A city hall, top quality, is about to host a visiting monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 reversed gives IA, which takes K inside to make IKA after SALON. Salonika is the older English name of Thessaloniki.
explanation.definitionFit: Salonika is the traditional English name for Thessaloniki, the second largest city in Greece.

clue.text: Indian worker adopting western divinity?

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for west or western
the name of God in Islam

explanation.surface: An Indian labourer taking up a Western religion.
explanation.definitionFit: In Indian English a wallah is a person doing a particular job, as in a chai wallah or punkah wallah.

clue.text: Be helpful as a bus conductor — or rude?

definitions.text: Be helpful as a bus conductor
definitions.meaning: literally, letting a passenger know which stop is theirs

definitions.note: an adjective standing for the rude act the verb phrase names
definitions.meaning: idiomatically, to rebuke ... sharply and put them in their place

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is a courteous service on a bus and a blunt telling-off elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to rebuke someone bluntly, while the literal sense is pointing a traveller to their stop.

clue.text: Sadly, Dorothy's without love and terribly sour

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Dolly is a pet form of the name Dorothy
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: something done terribly is mangled, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad story of Dorothy, lacking affection and feeling bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here it is the old sense of outside, so the pet name wraps everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolorously means in a sorrowful, mournful manner, an adverb of grief.

clue.text: Weak and ineffective insect swallowed a pair of bees

indicators.note: what is swallowed ends up inside the swallower

parts.note: a fly is an insect
taken as written
two of the letter B

explanation.surface: A feeble insect that has gulped down a couple of bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bees' are the letter B twice, not insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Flabby means slack and lacking firmness, figuratively feeble or lacking vigour.

clue.text: It might help, if you were to use your loaf!

definitions.text: It might help, if you were to use your loaf!

parts.words: It might help, if you were to use your loaf!
parts.note: surface reading: advice to think things through, as 'use your loaf' is slang for use your head
setter's reading: literally doing something with a loaf of bread, such as slicing it, which needs a board

explanation.walkthrough: 'Use your loaf' is British slang for think, from rhyming slang loaf of bread = head; taken literally, a cutting board helps.
explanation.definitionFit: A breadboard is the wooden board on which a loaf is placed for slicing.

clue.text: Port supplied by brother is poison

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for brother
taken as written
bane is an old word for poison, as in henbane

explanation.surface: A harbour town whose supply comes from a sibling who is toxic.
explanation.definitionFit: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland in Australia, a river port on Moreton Bay.

clue.text: See 10
Like the Unknown Soldier, demonstrating maleness in conflict

indicators.note: letters in conflict are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Unknown Soldier showed manly courage in war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Unknown Soldier is an unidentified war dead buried to honour all, so his name is not known.

clue.text: See 10
Structure on stern of ship is overweight when erected — and weak

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising a word up makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: fat means overweight
frail means weak

explanation.surface: A ship's stern fitting is too heavy once put up, yet flimsy.
explanation.definitionFit: A taffrail is the handrail or rail round the stern of a ship.

clue.text: More than one zone in Yorkshire countryside impresses deeply

indicators.note: the letters go in, placed inside the scenery word

parts.note: the Yorkshire Dales are a valley region of northern England
Z is an abbreviation for zone, so more than one is ZZ

explanation.surface: Several areas of Yorkshire landscape that make a strong impression on visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: DALES holds ZZ: DA-ZZ-LES. The Dales are a National Park of valleys in Yorkshire, a county in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To dazzle someone is to overwhelm them with admiration, so it strongly impresses them.

clue.text: University folk trained accountant the wrong way

indicators.note: going the wrong way means running backwards

parts.note: a gun trained on a target is aimed at it
Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants

explanation.surface: A trained accountant ends up in the wrong job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' looks like educated, but it means pointed, as a weapon is trained.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of higher education and the scholars who work in it, collectively.

clue.text: Composer sets down church composition at home

parts.note: the standard abbreviation for church
op. is short for opus, a musical work
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A composer writes down a piece of church music while at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederic Chopin was the Polish Romantic pianist famed for his piano works.

clue.text: See 10
One's against boastful talk? On the contrary!

definitions.text: One's against boastful talk? On the contrary!

indicators.note: the contrary order means the two parts swap places from how the words come

parts.note: gas is empty boastful chatter
con means against, as in pros and cons

explanation.surface: Someone who disapproves of bragging, or perhaps quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read straight, 'against boastful talk' gives CON GAS; 'On the contrary' swaps the order. Gascons were proverbially boastful, so far from being against bragging, a Gascon is all for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Natives of Gascony were famed as braggarts, giving the word gasconade, so a Gascon is a boaster.

clue.text: Respond to 999 calls? Get lost!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what firefighters do when called out to fires
second meaning: an angry dismissal telling someone to clear off

explanation.walkthrough: 999 is the British emergency telephone number, so a fire crew answering it literally heads to the fires.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old curse meaning go to hell, used as a rude brush-off, and literally a fire engine's journey.

clue.text: Warning number heard

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: four is a number

explanation.surface: A warning given by calling out a number.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers shout this cry to alert people in the path of a ball they have hit.

clue.text: Escaped one of the miseries of winter, it's said

indicators.note: said means we go by how the word is spoken, not spelt

parts.words: one of the miseries of winter
parts.note: influenza is a common winter illness

explanation.surface: Someone got away from one of winter's hardships.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew as the past tense of flee or fly can mean ran away or made off quickly.

clue.text: Misshapen rustic tree

indicators.note: a misshapen thing is bent out of form, so the letters take a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gnarled tree in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Citrus is the genus of trees bearing oranges, lemons and limes.

clue.text: Former holy books man intended to be for all (not just disciples)

definitions.text: intended to be for all (not just disciples)

parts.note: ex means former
OT is the Old Testament
a man's name

explanation.surface: Old scriptures that a man meant to be read by everyone, not only the faithful.
explanation.definitionFit: Exoteric teaching is suitable for the general public, the opposite of esoteric doctrine reserved for initiates.
